An effective strategy is to equip an Eye of Ayak and be prepared to attack ranged nylocas as soon as they change. Without any additional magic damage bonus, this will always kill the nylocas in one hit as long as your current Magic level is at least 93.

In phase 2, these are always accompanied by a Nylocas Athanatos. It is recommended to keep the Athanatos alive, as its presence will prevent any additional nylocas from spawning until 35.0% or less health, where two Nylocas Matomenos begin to periodically spawn. The healing that the Athanatos provides can generally be outpaced by the team.

In phase 3, they appear as Verzik's first special attack (after 4 auto attacks), and will not be used until 16 auto-attacks later when she loops her special attack rotation again. These should be killed off as soon as they spawn.
Even though it's not specifically stated, you cannot die yourself during this task. If you die during Verzik the task will not complete for you, but it will for the rest of the team.

tasks.name: Team Work Makes the Dream Work
tasks.description: When Verzik Vitur in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode uses her yellow power blast attack while the tornadoes are active, have everyone get through the attack without taking damage. This cannot be completed with one player alive
context: Team Work Makes the Dream Work is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to have everyone get through the attack without taking damage when Verzik Vitur, in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode, uses her yellow power blast attack while the tornadoes are active. This cannot be completed with one player alive.

tasks.name: Harder Mode III
tasks.description: Defeat Verzik Vitur in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode without anyone attacking her with a melee weapon during her third phase.
context: Harder Mode III is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Verzik Vitur in hard mode without using melee weapons during her third phase.
method: The player has the option to choose between the staff of the dead (as it is considered a magic weapon), a twisted bow or Tumeken's shadow for this achievement.

Verzik has a Defence level of 150 along with +30 slash, +100 magic and +230 ranged defence bonuses. Verzik's magic defence rolls off her Defence level rather than Magic in a manner similar to the ice demon, which can make Tumeken's shadow more consistent and high-hitting. It is best to avoid brewing whenever possible however, as this will reduce its effectiveness.
As long as the player does not die against Verzik, the achievement will be gained.

tasks.name: Pack Like a Yak
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode within the challenge time, with no deaths and without anyone buying anything from a supply chest.
context: Pack Like a Yak is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode raid within the challenge time, without anyone dying and without buying anything from the supply chest.
method: A stamina potion may be helpful to bring for both the Nylocas room and Verzik's fight. Only 1-2 players need to bring one with Boost Potion Share if they share the doses before the Nylocas room and/or before Verzik's web attack.

Players should try to only use supplies at the Nylocas and Verzik's fight. Prayer potions might be needed at the Maiden, Bloat and Sotetseg if necessary, but do not waste too much as the supplies will be needed for Verzik. Plan on saving at least 3 Saradomin brews and 3 Super restores for Verzik's fight in case of mistakes, meaning you should try to bring at least 4 brews and 4 restores into the raid to be safe.

Avoid extra hits at bloat if they would result in tanking flies or stomps. Bring an extra brew and hard food for emergencies and to heal before Nylocas Vasilias or during the waves Time Sotetseg's death ball with his shadow maze attack to remove the need to heal off its damage or camp low hitpoints.

tasks.name: Hard Mode? Completed It
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode within the challenge time.
context: Hard Mode? Completed It is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode within the challenge time.
method: Completing the raid in the challenge time is easiest in a group of 4 or 5. Time between the rooms is also counted, so players should avoid spending too much time waiting on teammates and buying supplies.

tasks.name: Theatre: HM (Trio) Speed-Runner
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode (Trio) with an overall time of less than 23 minutes.
context: Theatre: HM (Trio) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode in a team of 3 players with an overall time of less than 23 minutes.

tasks.name: Theatre: HM (4-Scale) Speed-Runner
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode (4-scale) with an overall time of less than 21 minutes.
context: Theatre: HM (4-Scale) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode in a team of 4 players with an overall time of less than 21 minutes.
Like other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.

tasks.name: Theatre: HM (5-Scale) Speed-Runner
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode (5-scale) with an overall time of less than 19 minutes.
context: Theatre: HM (5-Scale) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode in a team of 5 players with an overall time of less than 19 minutes.
Like other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.

tasks.name: Theatre of Blood: HM Grandmaster
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode 50 times.
context: Theatre of Blood: HM Grandmaster is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode 50 times.

tasks.name: Anticoagulants
tasks.description: Defeat the Maiden of Sugadinti in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without letting any bloodspawn live for longer than 10 seconds.
context: Anticoagulants is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Maiden of Sugadinti in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without letting a blood spawn live for more than 10 seconds.
method: If a blood spawn appears, immediately focus it down. Otherwise, killing the Maiden before she can summon them will also complete the achievement.

You do not need to complete the raid to complete the combat task. As the maiden is always the first boss you fight in a raid, you can complete the task in your best range gear and just resign to exit the raid. Taking only your range gear without any other gear switches means you can have an inventory with maximum food and pots. This allows a fairly easy fight and a quick way to complete the task.

tasks.name: Appropriate Tools
tasks.description: Defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode with everyone having a salve amulet equipped.
context: Appropriate Tools is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode with everyone having a salve amulet equipped.
This achievement can be completed with any version of the salve amulet.

tasks.name: They Won't Expect This
tasks.description: In the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, enter the Pestilent Bloat room from the opposite side.
context: They Won't Expect This is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, enter the Pestilent Bloat room from the opposite side.
method: This combat task is as easy as it sounds. You just need to enter the arena on the opposite side from where you enter.

You do not need to finish the raid to complete the combat task. Therefore, if you just leave the raid after entering the arena you can greatly simplify your setup and inventory by just using your best range gear to quickly defeat the maiden, who is always the first boss you will encounter and not bothering to fight the Pestilent Bloat. Useful if you just need 4 combat points to achieve the next combat achievement.

However, it is worth attempting to fight the Pestilent Bloat and try to complete the Appropriate Tools and Chally Time combat tasks by bringing some melee gear and a suitable halberd. (See Theatre of Blood/Strategies for suggest setups you can adapt.)
Completing these 3 fairly easy tasks will reward 12 combat task points and help you on to the next combat achievement reward.

tasks.name: Chally Time
tasks.description: Defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode by using a halberd special attack as your final attack.
context: Chally Time is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode by using a dragon halberd or crystal halberd special attack as your final attack.
method: You do not need to complete the raid to complete the combat task. Therefore, if you just leave the raid after defeating the Pestilent Bloat you can simplify your inventory as the mage gear switch required for later in the raid will not be required. Your inventory can thus hold more food and potions to get you through the task.

It is advisable to take your best range gear to quickly defeat the maiden, who is always the first boss you will encounter, (consider completing the Anticoagulants achievement at this time), then switch to your best melee gear with a suitable halberd to complete this task by killing the Pestilent Bloat with a halberd special attack. (See Theatre of Blood/Strategies for suggest setups you can adapt.)

The They Won't Expect This and Appropriate Tools task can also be easily achieved at the same time as this task. So if you are looking for a few points to get to the next combat achievement unlock, completing these 3 tasks will reward 12 combat task points and help you on to the next combat achievement reward.

tasks.name: Nylocas, On the Rocks
tasks.description: In the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, freeze any 4 Nylocas with a single Ice Barrage spell.
context: Nylocas, On the Rocks is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to freeze any 4 nylocas with a single Ice Barrage spell during a Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode raid. As the achievement is completed immediately after freezing 4 nylocas, the raid does not need to be completed.
method: The easiest way to complete this achievement is to wait until at least halfway through the Nylocas encounter. When there are enough Nylocas stacked around a pillar, casting Ice barrage on the group will likely complete the achievement.

During Maiden, in groups of 2 or more, there is a chance that the South 4,5 and North 4,5 Matomenos will all spawn. They will clump together after a few seconds and can be frozen in unison, easily completing the achievement.

tasks.name: Just To Be Safe
tasks.description: Defeat Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode after having split the big ball with your entire team. This must be done with a group size of at least 2.
context: Just To Be Safe is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode after having split the big ball with your entire team. This must be done with a group size of at least 2.

The big ball refers to the special attack by Sotetseg where it launches a big red ball that cannot be protected against. When multiple players stand on the same tile, the damage inflicted from the ball is split between the players. This attack is used after Sotetseg launches at least ten magic attacks. *Please note: should you fail to split any of the big ball attacks you must restart the entire raid (you cannot simply die and restart this room). It is advised to turn on Combat Achievement Tasks Failure message.*

tasks.name: Don't Look at Me!
tasks.description: Kill Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without him reflecting any damage to anyone.
context: Don't Look at Me! is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without him reflecting any damage to anyone.

If you fail this achievement, dying and restarting the fight will not reset it. You must begin a new raid. It may be helpful to use a slower weapon, attacking only once or twice per Xarpus's turn, to not fail. Using a blowpipe may cause accidental attacks.

tasks.name: No-Pillar
tasks.description: Survive Verzik Vitur's pillar phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without losing a single pillar.
context: No-Pillar is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to survive Verzik Vitur's pillar phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without losing a single pillar.
method: Have every player use the Dawnbringer's special attack multiple times to quickly end the encounter. Avoid teammates spreading between multiple pillars. If one pillar is taking too much damage, preemptively move to another.

tasks.name: Attack, Step, Wait
tasks.description: Survive Verzik Vitur's second phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without anyone getting bounced by Verzik.
context: Attack, Step, Wait is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to survive Verzik Vitur's second phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without anyone getting bounced by Verzik.
method: If you fail this achievement you can die and re-attempt Verzik within the same raid. You do not need to fully complete the raid to finish this task; you must simply defeat Verzik's 2nd phase without getting bounced.

tasks.name: Pass It On
tasks.description: In the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, successfully pass on the green ball to a team mate.
context: Pass It On is an elite combat achievement which requires the player in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, to successfully pass on the green ball to a team mate.
The green ball is a special attack launched by Verzik Vitur in her third phase.
method: The ball must either target the player or be passed from another teammate in order to attempt to pass it to another player. Once the ball is targeting the player, stand near another player to bounce the ball and complete the achievement. Right-click following another player is an easy way to stay close to them.

tasks.name: Theatre of Blood: SM Speed-Chaser
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode in less than 17 minutes.
context: Theatre of Blood: SM Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete an Entry Mode Theatre of Blood run within 17 minutes, not including time between rooms. This can be completed with any group size.
method: Entry mode should prove to be no problem for most players; the only issue will be the Nylocas room and it is recommended to run a trio so the room can be cleared without much hassle.

tasks.name: Theatre of Blood: SM Adept
tasks.description: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode 1 time.
context: Theatre of Blood: SM Adept is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode 1 time.

tasks.name: Into the Den of Giants
tasks.description: Kill a Hill Giant, Moss Giant and Fire Giant in the Giant Cave within the Shayzien region.
context: Into the Den of Giants is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a hill giant, moss giant, and a fire giant in the Giants' Den within the Shayzien region.

The Giants' Den is in north-west Shayzien on the south-east side of Lake Molch. The closest teleport is fairy ring code . Players can also use the Shayzien teleport in the Kharedst's memoirs/Book of the Dead and run west.
Category:Hill Giant achievements Category:Moss Giant achievements Category:Fire Giant achievements

tasks.name: Sit Back and Relax
tasks.description: Deal 100 damage to creatures using undead thralls.
context: Sit Back and Relax is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to deal 100 damage to creatures using undead thralls. This can be accomplished accumulatively across multiple undead thrall casts and multiple enemies.

tasks.name: Phosani's Veteran
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare once.
context: Phosani's Veteran is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare once.

tasks.name: Phosani's Master
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare 5 times.
context: Phosani's Master is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare 5 times.

tasks.name: Phosani's Grandmaster
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare 25 times.
context: Phosani's Grandmaster is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare 25 times.

tasks.name: Perfect Phosani's Nightmare
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare while only taking damage from husks, power blasts and weakened Parasites. Also, without having your attacks slowed by the Nightmare Spores or letting a Sleepwalker reach Phosani's Nightmare.
context: Perfect Phosani's Nightmare is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare while only taking damage from husks, weakened parasites and power blasts while also not getting slowed by spores or letting a sleepwalker reach her.
method: The task is fairly achievable as the player should always be aiming to achieve a perfect kill anyway, as any mistakes result in harsh damage dealt.
Mechanically, the largest threat is Spores, as each spore has a 3x3 AoE, meaning the player must be careful while navigating across totems.
Because the task also requires no sleepwalkers to reach the boss, Dreamland Express is mandatory.

tasks.name: Phosani's Speedchaser
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare within 7 minutes and 30 seconds.
context: Phosani's Speedchaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare in under 7 minutes and 30 seconds.
method: For strategies on this achievement, see Phosani's Speedrunner.

tasks.name: Phosani's Speedrunner
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare within 6 minutes.
context: Phosani's Speedrunner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare in under 6 minutes.
method: Good gear is required for the achievement. Scythe of Vitur with Inquisitor's armour is recommended, but an Inquisitor's mace or Soulreaper axe with Bandos armour will suffice to make time. For the totems, full magic switch and a Tumeken's shadow or an Eye of Ayak are also recommended. Although very unlikely, it is realistically possible over hundreds of kills with an abyssal bludgeon and trident of the swamp as well, although this requires good execution of mechanics, a great deal of luck, and saving time whenever possible (such as eating in between phases). A Crimson kisten or Voidwaker is helpful for its consistent and high-damage special attacks.

There are some strategies that may be used to save time beyond standard execution and minimising time wasted: Using a Scythe of Vitur to deal the finishing blow on the last totem of each phase; this causes it to register as charged one tick sooner due to the overkill hitsplat Using a ham joint on husks and elder maul/godsword (on crush) on the parasites to immediately kill them with minimal ticks wasted Using a lightbearer to perform additional special attacks in the overall fight, Death Charge on husks, parasites or sleepwalkers and bringing an ultor ring switch Running to where Phosani's Nightmare will be after her surge attack to resume attacking her immediately
As the boss is located in an instance, players going specifically for this achievement may opt to reset the fight if the start is slow.

tasks.name: Crush Hour
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare while killing every parasite and husk in one hit.
context: Crush Hour is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare while killing every husk and parasite that appears in a single hit.
method: Both the husk and parasite will take damage equal to the player's maximum hit if a weapon with a crush attack style is used to attack them. Husks have 20 health and can be instantly killed by most forms of crush-based weaponry, while Parasites have 55 health, which can be dealt with using a strong two-handed weapon like a godsword, elder maul, soulreaper axe or the special attack of the dragon mace. The unweakened variant gains extra health, which is too high for these weapons.
Note that if a thrall attacks either at the same time the player does, the achievement will fail.

tasks.name: I Would Simply React
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare without allowing your prayer to be disabled.
context: I Would Simply React is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare without having it disable their prayers.
method: The prayer disabling mechanic only takes place in phase 3, doing so prior to launching an incoming attack; players need only deactivate their protection prayer right after the attack lands.

tasks.name: Dreamland Express
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare without a sleepwalker reaching her during her desperation phase.
context: Dreamland Express is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Phosani's Nightmare without a sleepwalker reaching her during her desperation phase and damaging the player.
method: The Nightmare in phase 4 will have 150 health. Acceptable special attacks include the crimson kisten, Voidwaker, dragon claws, and granite maul (with an ornate maul handle attached) in that order. The kisten is the most consistent of the four due to taking advantage of the Nightmare's weakness to crush, while the Voidwaker is only slightly worse than it due to the lower damage range despite having a higher max hit and guaranteed accuracy.

The first sleepwalker will spawn as soon as the phase begins, and will reach the Nightmare in ~15 game ticks, damaging the player around ~17-18 ticks. This will allow for four attacks with a 4-tick weapon such as an Inquisitor's mace, or three with a Scythe of Vitur. With high-hitting special attacks, the player should be able to subdue the Nightmare before the first sleepwalker even reaches her.

If the sleepwalker ends up reaching the Nightmare, the player is only disqualified if pink petals fall on the player, as this indicates damage was inflicted. If these petals do not appear as the Nightmare is subdued, the player will not be damaged.

tasks.name: Can't Wake Up
tasks.description: Kill Phosani's Nightmare 5 times in a row without leaving Phosani's Dream.
context: Can't Wake Up is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare five times in a row without leaving her dream.
method: With a proper Phosani's Nightmare kill, the player's only source of damage should come from sleepwalkers at the end of phases 1-3, parasites when they burst from the player, and any sleepwalkers that reach Phosani's Nightmare during phase 4.

Since the player's inventory will be full of prayer restoration potions, this will leave them with no food to recover from mistakes. Ideal substitutes to restore health from chip damage and minor mistakes should be done with an amulet of blood fury, Sanguinesti staff, and a Saradomin godsword. The latter requires special attack energy however, and has to be used on a parasite, sleepwalker or husk to get the most out of it.

Phosani's Nightmare can provide some supplies in the form of Saradomin brews, prayer potions, Sanfew serums, bass, and sharks, which will last for 30 minutes in the instance. As the player should generally take minimal or no damage from mechanics, prayer potions and Sanfew serums are much more vital for the achievement. Try to line a kill up with food or potion drops, depending on what is brought more. Food is more common than potions, so it may be best to start with a full inventory of potions rather than food.

A Scythe of Vitur can generally be seen as a more effective choice than an Inquisitor's mace due to the two extra hits made per attack, though it is less accurate, and players would need to bring a ham joint to kill off the husks.

An ideal kill would generally take around 5-6 minutes (primarily depending overall performance) and consumes around two 4-dose prayer potions (with moderate flicking) and two doses of divine super combat potion. For five kills, the player should bring three 4-dose divine combat potions and 11 or 12 Sanfew serums. Depending on the player's speed, they may use anywhere from 0-3 doses of sanfew serum per kill.

Alternatively, players can forgo magic equipment to allow for more inventory spaces for potions and food. A halberd swap is recommended for this as one of the spore layouts will prevent players from using melee without running into one.

tasks.name: Nex Veteran
tasks.description: Kill Nex once.
context: Nex Veteran is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Nex once.

tasks.name: Nex Master
tasks.description: Kill Nex 25 times.
context: Nex Master is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Nex 25 times.
method: This achievement can be quickly completed by joining the any of the Nex mass worlds.

tasks.name: Nex Survivors
tasks.description: Kill Nex without anyone dying.
context: Nex Survivors is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Nex without having anyone die during the fight.

tasks.name: A siphon will solve this
tasks.description: Kill Nex without letting her heal from her Blood Siphon special attack.
context: A siphon will solve this is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without letting her heal from her Blood Siphon special attack.
method: Players must not attack Nex after she shouts as any damage done during that period will heal her instead. Any Blood Reavers that spawn must also be killed before she uses the special attack again.

tasks.name: Contain this!
tasks.description: Kill Nex without anyone taking damage from any Ice special attack.
context: Contain this! is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without having anyone take damage from her Containment and Ice Prison attacks.
method: Players must stay away from melee distance upon her using her Containment attack and quickly free any imprisoned teammates upon her using her Ice Prison attack. Both Osmumten's fang and Dragon warhammer are particularly accurate against the ice walls, but any crush weapon will work well.

tasks.name: There is no escape!
tasks.description: Kill Nex without anyone being hit by the Smoke Dash special attack.
context: There is no escape! is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without having anyone take damage from her Smoke Dash attack.
method: Players can avoid this attack by standing on the outside of the arena before the attack. If standing in melee distance, Nex will look at the direction she intends to dash towards prior to the attack as a warning indicator to avoid that lane.

tasks.name: Nex Trio
tasks.description: Kill Nex with three or less players at the start of the fight.
context: Nex Trio is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Nex with three or less players inside the arena at the start of the fight.

tasks.name: Nex Duo
tasks.description: Kill Nex with two or less players at the start of the fight.
context: Nex Duo is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex with only two or less players.
The task must be completed while there are two or less players in Nex's prison at the start of the fight.

tasks.name: I should see a doctor
tasks.description: Kill Nex whilst a player is coughing.
context: I should see a doctor is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires players to get kill credit for Nex while a player is infected with Nex's Choke attack.
method: For the task to be completed, players must purposely spread the virus to other players for the entirety of the fight. Players will cough four times (three with a slayer helmet) for each cough, which resets if they infect another player with it. The best way to complete the achievement is to have two or three players purposely infect each other while the rest of the team takes down Nex. These players should ideally not engage Nex in battle to avoid spreading the virus to other players who will be killing Nex.

tasks.name: Perfect Nex
tasks.description: Kill Nex whilst completing the requirements for "There is no escape", "Shadows move", "A siphon will solve this", and "Contain this!"
context: Perfect Nex is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex while qualifying for the completion of the following tasks: There is no escape!, Shadows Move..., A siphon will solve this, and Contain this!.

This means the player must kill Nex without anyone doing the following: Taking damage from Nex's Smoke Dash, Shadow Smash, Containment, and Ice Prison attacks Attacking Nex whilst she is performing her Blood Siphon attack
Despite being a grandmaster task, it can be attempted with any amount of players. If attempting in a large group, communication is helpful to avoid failing the achievement.

tasks.name: Shadows Move...
tasks.description: Kill Nex without anyone being hit by the Shadow Smash attack.
context: Shadows Move... is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without anyone being hit by her Shadow Smash attack.
Upon the shadows appearing beneath the player, they will have three ticks (1.8 seconds) to move out of it before they erupt and damage the player.

tasks.name: Tombs Speed Runner
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut (normal) within 18 mins at any group size.
context: Tombs Speed Runner is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid within 18 mins at any group size, at level 150 or above.
method: When attempting to complete the combat achievement, the following are the approximate times which the player should aim for each stage of the raid:

Gear Recommendations, for a duo, include max armour for all 3 combat styles: Torva, Masori, and Ancestral. Twisted Bow, Dragon Arrows, Blowpipe, Zaryte Crossbow, Tumeken's Shadow, Avernic Defender, Dragon Dagger, Dragon Claws, and one player with Thralls with the other player on the Lunar Spellbook for Vengeance/Vengeance Other. Both players could also use the Lunar Spellbook and use spellbook swap to use Thralls and Vengeance.

tasks.name: Tombs Speed Runner II
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut (expert) within 20 mins at any group size.
context: Tombs Speed Runner II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid within 20 minutes, with any group size, at level 300 or above.

This task is usually not done directly, instead, at the same time as Tombs Speed Runner III, as completing that task will satisfy this task. However, with strong enough gear and experience, this task can be easily completed on its own at a 300 raid level.
Hit 300 raid level while not using any path invocations, do use a 25 minute timer and hardcore. Avoid Medic, More Overlords, and Double Trouble, as they significantly slow the raid down.

Use thralls. Spellbook swapping can be useful but is not necessary in max. Every path boss and Wardens' P2 can be venged. Bring a pickaxe and an empty slot to avoid inventory management issues. Use liquid adrenaline, death charge, and a surge potion to constantly use burning claws, zaryte crossbow, or voidwaker special attacks. Death charge baba baboons if they are in a good spot (they are 1 ticked), pre-death charge kephri (swarms, overlords), and pre-death charge Akkha (shadows). P2 Core can be death charged during the first down, it can only be death charged during the final down if you kill it on the last hit.

Swarm both of Kephri's phases. Butterfly Akkha to ensure he stays in melee. If you do not have a ZCB, spec shadows with your melee spec as you transition quadrants. If on lunars, pre-vengeance. When Akkha is low hp(~around 150 health if shadowing), tank an off prayer, cast vengeance, and tank another off prayer. Two down P2 via dragon dagger special attacks.
Kill skulls during P3, attack from melee range.

tasks.name: Tombs Speed Runner III
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut (expert) within 18 mins in a group of 8.
context: Tombs Speed Runner III is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid in an 8-man party within 18 minutes, at raid level 300 or above.
Unlike the Theatre of Blood, speed-based achievements for the Tombs of Amascut count the overall time rather than the challenge time.
Like other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.
method: All players should ideally have a high Mining level to clear Het's challenge in one cycle to avoid wasting extra time with the 1-tick pre-mining method to get an additional hit in. All players are required to have near or best-in-slot gear as players must burst through the bosses very quickly. The bosses will have ~5.78 times the amount of health they would in solo. As it is important to move fast in between rooms it is also recommended to leave some inventory space, as to not have to drop and pick up items. With proper play food won't be needed until Wardens, where one should use Ambrosia.
Selecting easy invocations will minimise frustration during the attempt, and it is important that players do not die during the bosses, as even one player dying can significantly set the team back.

The zaryte crossbow with Ruby dragon bolts (e) can deal a lot of damage with its special attack. One player should bring an elder maul or dragon warhammer, while another brings a soulflame horn to make Ba-Ba and Kephri easier to handle. A player can bring a Keris partisan of corruption to use its special attack to allow teammates to deal more damage for a short duration.

Another option is for the whole team to camp mage and use Eye of Ayak's special attack at the start of each boss, with the exception of Akkha, who can be zaryte crossbow specced thrice with liquid adrenaline and surge potion.

The baboons in Apmeken's challenge are very straightforward following the changes on 24 May 2024 and 25 June 2025, as players are guaranteed max hits on combat baboons and specialist baboons barely have any health.

Ba-Ba should be dragged as close to the southern end of the arena as possible reduce the amount of time spent falling after her roar. The baboons should be ignored to send her to the next phase as soon as possible.

The path of Crondis can be sped up by synchronizing the collection of the water jugs, bypassing the respawn time on the waterfalls and avoiding any damage to the Palm of Resourcefulness from the crocodiles. Having a person enter with the "Pass" option instead of "Quick-Pass", whilst the rest of the team spams "Pass", guarantees everyone to be synced up.
Zebak's fight is fairly straightforward. Minimize time spent pushing water jugs and avoiding waves.

For Kephri, two or three players should act as swarm killers, killing the scarab swarms that appear during the interlude phases to minimise the amount of healing Kephri can recover; if done properly, she will only recover with 1 health, often resulting in the next hit putting her out. On the 2nd phase, kill the Soldier Scarab as soon as possible to limit healing while keeping the Arcane Scarab from attacking.

At Akkha, one player should serve as a butterfly, kiting Akkha so that he never gets the chance to attack the team. It is recommended to have Feeling Special active, so the memory blast attack can be performed faster. Use Tumeken's shadow on him unless he enters his magic stance, after which players should begin using a fang instead.
The Wardens can be completed as normal. Try to clear the second phase within two core downs, ideally with Tumeken's Warden being fought for the last two phases.
Assuming a normal raid level of 300 with no path levelling, the enemies will have the following health:
Zebak: 7400 Kephri: 1910 (shield), 1020 (unguarded) Akkha: 5100 Ba-Ba: 4850 Obelisk: 3320 Wardens: 1790 (shield), 33930 (core), 11230 (phase 3) Skulls: 4

tasks.name: You are not prepared
tasks.description: Complete a full Tombs of Amascut raid only using supplies given inside the tomb and without anyone dying.
context: You are not prepared is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid using only supplies provided by the Helpful Spirit without dying, at level 150 or above. The task will fail if any players in the raid use outside supplies.
method: Players should pre-pot (including with an extended anti-venom+) before entering the raid. Using a Falador shield to restore prayer and the Keris partisan of the sun special attack or Blood Spells to restore health will not fail the task. Health, prayer, run energy and special attack are also restored after clearing each path.

It is recommended to prioritise taking nectar and tears of Elidinis from the Helpful Spirit. Ambrosia is also useful as it is the only way to cure poison or venom. Start with Zebak and Kephri first since they can be cleared with little damage taken, then take care to avoid the Cursed Baboon's venom trails in the Path of Apmeken.

tasks.name: Helpful spirit who?
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut without using any supplies from the Helpful Spirit and without anyone dying. Honey locusts are included in this restriction.
context: Helpful spirit who? is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid at level 150 or above without relying on the Helpful Spirit for supplies. The raid must be completed deathless by the entire party and will fail if any players in the raid use supplies from the Helpful Spirit.
method: Bring a 4-dose potion of super combat and ranging. For a magic boost, bring an imbued or saturated heart instead. Ancient and forgotten brews can be used in place of the heart, but this will drain melee stats in the process.

As the player will not have access to smelling salts and liquid adrenaline, be prepared to three cycle the Warden on phase 2. Other than that, the bosses can be killed fairly easily on a raid level of 150 with good gear.

tasks.name: Resourceful Raider
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut with the "On a diet" and "Dehydration" invocations activated and without anyone dying.
context: Resourceful Raider is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid while having the "Dehydration" and "On a Diet" invocation on and no players dying, at level 300 or above.
method: To complete this task, it is highly recommended that the player has an amulet of blood fury and Keris partisan of the sun. A Sanguinesti staff is helpful, but not absolutely required if the player possesses Tumeken's shadow.

On a Diet prevents players from using solids (e.g sharks) and also prevents the Helpful Spirit from giving Silk dressings. Dehydration prevents players from using potions to heal (e.g Saradomin brews), which also means that players cannot use nectar or ambrosia either.

The only bosses where players may take significant damage would be Wardens and Akkha, as Zebak, Kephri and Ba-Ba should not deal any significant damage at all due to their attacks being easily avoidable and/or blocked. The player's main source of healing will be from the sun keris, as its passive restores 12 health and overheals to 20% of their base Hitpoints level at the cost of 5 prayer points. This effect is particularly useful at the Wardens' phase 3 to heal off the skulls during the interludes. In addition, it has a special attack that fully restores health and overheals 20% of their Hitpoints level at the cost of 50 prayer points, which can be very useful in a pinch.

The Saradomin Godsword and toxic blowpipe are also a viable option for providing healing power through the Wardens fight. Since "Dehydration" and "On a Diet" are active, the player should only select the "Power" option from the Helpful Spirit, which provides both a smelling salt and liquid adrenaline. The "Chaos" option is only useful if the pack contains adrenaline and tears of Elidinis, although this scenario is usually unlikely and thus players can simply choose another power option instead.
Due to the extra adrenaline, players can dump special attacks on whoever is the last boss to slightly speed up the kill time.

tasks.name: But... Damage
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut without anyone in your party wearing or holding any equipment at tier 75 or above.
context: But... Damage is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid without using any tier 75 or higher equipment, at level 300 or above.
method: As tier 75 or higher equipment cannot be used, players will be unable to use most reasonable weapons and equipment that would make the raid faster. The second-best alternatives to use in lieu of them would be the gear setup below.

If crystal armour is outside of your ability/price, hunters' sunlight crossbow, an odium ward and moonlight antler bolts are good alternatives to the crystal bow as the high attack speed can compensate for some of the accuracy and strength loss. Thralls are allowed. Burning Claws and Belle's Folly are eligible and can be brought in as a spec weapon and stab weapon respectively.

Unlike the tier 65 Keris partisan, the Keris partisan of the sun, Keris partisan of breaching, Keris partisan of amascut and Keris partisan of corruption cannot be brought into the raid as they require 80 Attack.

Below is an example equipment and inventory that can be used to complete this task. Quantities and ratios of supplies needed is very dependant on how experienced a player is with the Tombs of Amascut raid. Example inventory might not apply to everyone, and players should make adjustments based on their own skills.

Despite being equipment that is tier 75 or higher, the following items may currently be used without failing the task: Holy ghrazi rapier Holy sanguinesti staff Holy and Sanguine Scythe of Vitur Ancient sceptre with quartz attached Desert treasure 2 rings Max cape variants of Dizana's quiver Amulet of rancour (s) Echo Virtus robes
Lastly, dying does not disqualify the player for the task; as long as one teammate survives and completes the raid, the task is completed for all participants.

tasks.name: Chompington
tasks.description: Defeat Zebak using only melee attacks and without dying yourself.
context: Chompington is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Zebak using only melee attacks without dying, at raid level 150 or above. The achievement will be earned immediately after defeating Zebak so the raid does not need to be completed.
method: At the minimum raid level of 150, Zebak will have 930 health. Zebak's melee attack hits the hardest and can also apply a bleeding effect that deals additional damage if the player moves. Assuming no path levelling is active (which should most likely be the case), Zebak will have an attack speed of 7, or once every 4.2 seconds. Once he enrages, his attack speed increases to 4, or every 2.4 seconds.

Use the best melee weapons and armour you have access to, prioritising melee accuracy and strength bonuses over defensive bonuses. Defence reducing special attacks, such as the Bandos godsword's, can be used since like Ba-Ba he does not reset his Defence level. However, his Defence can only be lowered to 50 (from 70 and before modifications). He has fairly high defensive bonuses (+160 stab, slash and +260 crush), so Osmumten's fang is highly effective due to its passive effect. All melee damage from Zebak can be avoided by using a flinching method. This is done by attacking Zebak from three tiles away, and immediately after, running out of his melee attack range. Zebak's melee attack has a one tick delay, so if the player only stays in his melee range for one tick at a time, his melee attacks will never damage the player. Alternative, easier but slower, strategy is to use a crystal halberd or noxious halberd to attack him standing two tiles away causing him to never use his melee attack.

Note: Usage of ghostly and skeletal thralls, recoil damage (e.g. ring of recoil, Vengeance), and the Voidwaker's special attack will all fail the challenge. However, both zombie thralls and burn damage from Burning claws's special attack will not fail the challenge, and ranged weapons can be used to break the jugs.

tasks.name: Fancy feet
tasks.description: Complete phase three of The Wardens in a group of two or more, using only melee attacks and without dying yourself. The 'Insanity' invocation must be activated.
context: Fancy feet is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete phase three of The Wardens in a group of two or more, using only melee attacks and without dying, at raid level 300 or above. The 'Insanity' invocation must be activated.
method: Insanity can only be toggled on when both "Overclocked" and "Overclocked 2" are active, which when combined with "Insanity" will make the Warden attack every 3 ticks.

The Warden will have 1940 health per player at a raid level of 300, resulting in it having a total of 1940* party size health. Each slam attack will deal roughly 40-50 damage if not avoided. The player must move immediately after attacking to avoid getting hit by the slam, as there is no time to dodge the attack when within five tiles from the boss. The boss will also have four interlude phases entwined at 20% health intervals which release more Energy Siphons in a different layout compared to solo, however despite having "Insanity" there is still a larger amount of time to reverse the skulls before they explode. It is possible to survive with 80+ health with one skull untouched, but two or more result in instant death unless the player somehow manages to avoid the resulting explosion. Supply invocations should be left untouched, and this should leave players with a significant amount of supplies entering the Wardens.

When the Warden reaches critical health, it will restore 20% of its health and any drained Defence levels and increase its Defence. This will also cause one of the two phantom bosses (Ba-Ba's Phantom for Tumeken and Akkha's Phantom for Elidinis) to attack faster.

Players should use Osmumten's fang for the task, as it is the most accurate of melee weapons due to the passive effect it has while in the raid, despite the Warden's slightly higher stab resistance. To handle defence drains, one player should use a soulflame horn while the other uses a dragon warhammer or elder maul special attack, as this will reduce its Defence to the maximum; 30 drained levels pre-enrage and 60 post-enrage, significantly increasing accuracy.
Warning: While thralls can be used for this achievement, they must be zombified thralls; using ghostly or Skeletal thralls will cause disqualification.

tasks.name: Hardcore Raiders
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut in a group of two or more without anyone dying.
context: Hardcore Raiders is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid in a group of two or more without anyone dying, at raid level 150 or above.

tasks.name: Hardcore Tombs
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut solo without dying.
context: Hardcore Tombs is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid solo without dying, at level 150 or above. The Hardcore Run invocation does not need to be active in order to complete the achievement.

tasks.name: Perfect Het
tasks.description: Complete the Het room without taking any damage from the light beam and orbs. You must destroy the core after one exposure.
context: Perfect Het is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Het challenge room without taking any damage from the light beam or orbs, and destroying Het's Seal in one cycle, at raid level 150 or above.
method: Level 85 Mining (boostable from 82 with a Dragon pickaxe) is required for this task in a solo encounter in order to deal enough damage to Het's Seal in one cycle. There is more leeway in group encounters depending on the Mining level of the other teammates and if they are one-tick clicking the pillar before the beam hits the shielded statue, as this provides an extra hit to the statue before the next cycle starts (see Tombs of Amascut/Strategies for the one-cycle method).

The team should take time setting down mirrors to ensure that the beam won't hit them as they set it and watch out for any orbs that appear while setting the mirrors and mining the pillar, as they have a notorious habit of forcing players to move out of the way when the pillar is being destroyed.
A boosted Mining level of 100 or higher will allow destroying the core without the one-tick prep in a solo encounter.

tasks.name: Perfect Akkha
tasks.description: Complete Akkha in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Akkha's attacks off-prayer, Akkha's special attacks (orbs, memory, detonate), exploding shadow timers, orbs in the enrage phase or attacking Akkha with the wrong style. You must have all Akkha invocations activated.
context: Perfect Akkha is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete Akkha in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Akkha's attacks off-prayer, Akkha's special attacks (orbs, memory, detonate), exploding shadow timers, orbs in the enrage phase or attacking Akkha with the wrong style. The player must have all Akkha invocations activated.
method: Using a melee thrall in the final phase of the fight will fail this combat achievement. It is not known whether this is intended or a bug. However, as Akkha has a chance to change his combat style with every special, it is not recommended to use thralls when attempting this achievement, even if the player starting the encounter is confident with their "butterfly" technique.

As Double Trouble needs to be activated with multiple players, the player butterflying Akkha should dodge the memory attack in the middle, while other players should use the "staircase" technique to skip the memory attack at the edges of the arena. If Akkha switches styles and uses black orbs at the same time, it may be safer to stay still and flick protection prayers, rather than attempting to flinch.
Since the achievement is under Tombs of Amascut, the fastest method is to attempt the achievement with a raid level of 150 with all Akkha invocations active, reducing his health.

tasks.name: Perfection of Het
tasks.description: Complete 'Perfect Het' and 'Perfect Akkha' in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut.
context: Perfection of Het is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Het and Perfect Akkha in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut raid at raid level 300 or above.
method: Perfect Het and Perfect Akkha do not need to be completed in succession. As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Het and then fail Perfect Akkha can all die and re-attempt Perfect Akkha without having to redo Perfect Het.

tasks.name: Perfect Apmeken
tasks.description: Complete the Apmeken room in a group of two or more, without anyone allowing any dangers to trigger, standing in venom or being hit by a volatile baboon. You must complete this room in less than three minutes.
context: Perfect Apmeken is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Apmeken challenge room in a group of two or more without allowing any dangers to trigger, standing in venom, or being hit by a volatile baboon, while completing the room within three minutes, at raid level 150 or above.
method: Hammers and Neutralising potion are provided in crates in the room before the challenge can start.

When the first player enters the challenge area, they will obtain Apmeken's Sight, which allows them to identify dangers and resolve them before they damage the team. If the pillars have an issue, call out P; if the vents have an issue, call V. If corruption is spreading, death-dot (in larger groups) or use the potion on the corrupted player (smaller groups).

Freeze any Cursed Baboons and immediately kill them to avoid spreading venom. Volatile Baboons can be easily avoided as their explosion is a 3x3 AoE centered around them; they can also be killed, but it is not required.
Following the 29 May 2024 update to the Path of Apmeken, this achievement is significantly easier as the baboons have very little health and can be easily killed in one or a few hits.

tasks.name: Perfect Ba-Ba
tasks.description: Defeat Ba-Ba in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Ba-Ba's Attacks off-prayer, Ba-Ba's slam, rolling boulders, rubble attack or falling rocks. No sarcophagi may be opened. You must have all Ba-Ba invocations activated.
context: Perfect Ba-Ba is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba in a group of two or more, at raid level 150 or above, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Ba-Ba's Attacks off-prayer, Ba-Ba's slam, rolling boulders, rubble attack or falling rocks. No sarcophagi may be opened. The player must have all Ba-Ba invocations activated.
This Combat achievement CAN be re-attempted by wiping. This combat achievement is not failed if a player is struck by bananas.

tasks.name: Perfection of Apmeken
tasks.description: Complete 'Perfect Apmeken' and 'Perfect Ba-Ba' in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut.
context: Perfection of Apmeken is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Apmeken and Perfect Ba-Ba in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut raid at raid level 300 or above.
method: The Path of Apmeken does not need to be completed in 3 minutes, as is normally required for Perfect Apmeken. Additionally, it and Perfect Ba-Ba do not need to be completed in succession.
As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Apmeken and then fail Perfect Ba-Ba can all die and re-attempt Perfect Ba-Ba without having to redo Perfect Apmeken.

tasks.name: Perfect Crondis
tasks.description: Complete the Crondis room without letting a crocodile get to the tree, without anyone losing water from their container and in under one minute.
context: Perfect Crondis is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Crondis challenge room without letting a crocodile get to the tree, without anyone losing water from their container and in under one minute, at raid level 150 or above.
method: Since deaths restart this task, one (except hardcore iron men) may save a few ticks by entering the puzzle room just to get the water container, then dying to restart the task, as it will appear in the inventory after death. Also, in case one fails, a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake may be used to reset the task faster.

tasks.name: Perfect Zebak
tasks.description: Defeat Zebak without anyone taking any damage from: poison, Zebak's basic attacks off-prayer, blood spawns and waves. You also must not push more than two jugs on the roar attack during the fight (you may destroy stationary ones). You must have all Zebak invocations activated.
context: Perfect Zebak is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Zebak without taking any damage from incorrectly prayed attacks (excluding his blood magic), poison pools, blood spawns, and waves. All of his invocations must be activated to complete the task at raid level 150 or above.
method: As Upset Stomach will be active, remember to take note that the water jugs have a 3x3 AoE and acid pools 5x5.

Taking damage from Zebak's roar attack will not cause the achievement to fail, so it can be significantly easier to tank the roar attack each time it happens and focus on dealing damage instead of setting up the jugs. Make sure the tile in front of you and a few tiles behind you are clear to not get pushed into acid during the attack. If one is specifically going for this achievement and healing is a concern for tanking, one can simply disable any of the lives invocations and die repeatedly to Zebak with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake to obtain enough Honey locusts, which are stackable and can overheal above max health. Simply leave the raid after successfully completing the achievement.

With sufficient DPS, it's possible to skip one of the four special attacks Zebak would use, minimising the chances of failing the achievement as the acid pools are the only concern for the task. Standing next to the ramp to the water should avoid most if not all of the acid pools.
It is important to note that getting hit by the water jugs does not fail the achievement attempt.

tasks.name: Perfect Scabaras
tasks.description: Complete the Scabaras room in less than a minute without anyone taking any damage from puzzles.
context: Perfect Scabaras is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Scabaras challenge room in less than a minute without anyone taking any damage from puzzles, at raid level 150 or above.
method: The achievement is best done in a solo encounter while avoiding the pillars room, since this room is a guessing game and can take a while to solve. The last puzzle is incapable of damaging players. A fast way to reattempt the combat achievement is to log out of the raid and start a new raid.

tasks.name: Perfect Kephri
tasks.description: Defeat Kephri in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: egg explosions, Kephri's attacks, Exploding Scarabs, Bodyguards, dung attacks. No eggs may hatch throughout the fight.
context: Perfect Kephri is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Kephri in an group of two or more players without taking any damage from egg explosions, her auto-attacks, exploding scarabs, bodyguards (chip damage from range and melee bodyguards does not disqualify if prayed against, neither does poison damage) and dung attacks, at raid level 150 or above. In addition, players must not let any Agile Scarabs hatch.
Unlike Perfect Ba-Ba, Perfect Akkha, and Perfect Zebak, this combat achievement does not require any Kephri invocations to be enabled.

tasks.name: Perfection of Scabaras
tasks.description: Complete 'Perfect Scabaras' and 'Perfect Kephri' in a single run of Tombs of Amascut.
context: Perfection of Scabaras is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Scabaras and Perfect Kephri in a single Expert mode run of the Tombs of Amascut raid.
method: Path of Scabaras does not need to be completed in less than 1 min, as is normally required for Perfect Scabaras. Additionally, Perfect Scabaras and Perfect Kephri do not need to be completed in succession.
As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Scabaras and then fail Perfect Kephri can all die and re-attempt Perfect Kephri without having to redo Perfect Scabaras.

tasks.name: Perfect Wardens
tasks.description: Defeat The Wardens in a group of two or more, without anyone taking avoidable damage from the following: Warden attacks, obelisk attacks, lightning attacks in phase three, skull attack in phase three, Demi god attacks in phase three. You must have all Wardens invocations activated.
context: Perfect Wardens is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Wardens in a group of at least two players, while not taking damage from any avoidable attacks, while having all of their invocations enabled, at raid level 150 or above.
method: Phase 1 has two possible attacks that will disqualify the player - standing next to the obelisk when it is destroyed causes an explosion that will fail the task, as well as getting hit by the pyramids that come down.

Phase 2 begins to introduce attacks that will disqualify the player if they are not dealt with. For the purposes of this task, Elidinis' Warden should be fought instead of Tumeken's Warden as it will not try to chase after players, so they can focus solely on using Protect from Missiles or Protect from Magic. Tumeken's phantoms are also significantly easier to handle. Red skulls indicate a magic attack, while plain skulls indicate a ranged attack. The Warden will also launch prayer-disabling projectiles in the form of a scimitar, arrow or orb, in which Protect from Melee/Ranged/Magic should be used to block the attack. Failing to pray against the attacks will disqualify the players from the achievement.

The obelisk will also cycle between three special attacks for the duration of phase 2, Windmill, Lightning and Converging Beam. The attacks can be easily avoided by making the most of the tiles to find safe spots.

Phase 3 is the hardest part of the achievement, especially in the enrage phase since getting hit by a lightning attack will immediately disqualify the player. As with the Warden attacks, make sure to pray against the attacks from the first phantom. In a normal level 150 raid, the Warden will only have 2560 health in a duo encounter and will be quite easy to defeat in high-level gear.

This task can be done with alt account as +1, but requires alt account to log out during p1 and log back in once the p3 has started. If alt account never enters into p1/p2, they will be spawned into the fight when p3 starts. Logging out and back in circumvents that and still doesn't count as death for the purpose of this task.

tasks.name: Insanity
tasks.description: Complete 'Perfect Wardens' at expert or above.
context: Insanity is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Wardens in the Tombs of Amascut raid at level 300 or above.
method: As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players can all die and re-attempt Wardens without having to redo the entire raid.

tasks.name: Amascut's Remnant
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut at raid level 500 or above without anyone dying.
context: Amascut's Remnant is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid at level 500 or above without anyone dying.
method: A raid level of 500 will increase the enemies' stats by 200% and health by 150%, making each boss somewhat challenging in itself.
Learning how to use various advanced tactics will help significantly in the raid, as conserving supplies for the Wardens is essential to successfully complete the task.

A Tumeken's shadow is the most powerful weapon in the Tombs of Amascut and will make a 500 run much easier, enabling tactics such as Butterfly Akkha, and doing enough damage to defeat Akkha's Shadows quickly or end Warden's enrage phase early. See Tombs of Amascut/Strategies for a breakdown of the best weapons for each encounter. The next best weapons for Wardens are the Twisted bow and Bow of Faerdhinen. An Osmumten's fang is all but required for Kephri and Ba-ba.

Since the Keris partisan of the sun is likely going to be your only form of healing due to 'Dehydration' and 'No help needed', the amount of Super restores you bring in will be the only supplies you will have access to for the entire raid. It is highly recommended that players get a jewel of the sun before attempting this achievement, as with 'Dehydration' active, the player will have very limited forms of healing that will likely cost dps and supplies if they are brought along.

Taking Power both times from the Helpful Spirit might be necessary, as Liquid adrenaline potions are vital for being able to heal multiple times and two salts possibly being needed if the last two bosses are slow. If prayer is a problem, Life can be useful for the tears and scarab.
An Amulet of blood fury helps sustain chip damage during Kephri and Akkha, occasionally reducing the need to Keris spec. Otherwise, an Amulet of rancour or amulet of torture are beneficial.

Balance additional gear switches with extra prayer potions to ensure you can complete the raid while still allowing for mistakes. Combining gear where possible, such as using Mixed hide armour as your range and melee armour, Barrows gloves as your melee and range gloves, or using Blue moon armour as your melee and mage armour can free up valuable inventory space without losing too much dps.

If Ba-ba and Kephri are done first in order, you only need to bring a single Super combat potion to handle both rooms effectively. An Antidote++ can be used before the raid begins and will likely last until the end of Kephri's room.

As most invocations need to be active to reach 500 invocation level, there are only a few options available to make the run as easy as possible. It is almost guaranteed your invocation list will contain 'No help needed', 'Dehydration', 'Insanity', and many boss invocations.
Invocations to avoid:

'Quiet prayers', as it will drain far too many supplies throughout a raid while also potentially killing the player in places they normally would survive. 'Medic!', as it can waste a lot of time, (upwards of 2-3 minutes), at Kephri and will drain a noticeable amount of supplies. Any of the time invocations will add unnecessary stress and potentially fail the challenge run on a successful clear if the time is not met.
Some difficult invocations to consider adding or removing.

'Overly draining' will limit your damage dealing special attacks and healing potential with the Keris partisan of the sun, adding time to the raid and limiting mistakes. 'Double trouble' will interrupt Akkha more frequently and add time to the run, and requires advanced movement alongside 'Feeling special'. 'Keep back' will add additional chip damage or movement to an already challenging room, but is otherwise manageable. Can be almost completely ignored with the butterfly technique and a Tumeken's shadow or bow of Faerdhinen. 'Pathmaster' pushes each Boss to level 3 at a minimum, increasing their stats and adding additional mechanics. Although it usually won't change any strategies, it will add extra time to each room. Level 4 Zebak is notoriously challenging and should be avoided if possible. 'Ancient haste' can add a lot of unavoidable damage during P1 wardens. Less dps in this phase can drain supplies more than expected, but can be mitigated with Redemption and Tick eating strategies. 'More overlords' will add extra time to Kephri, requiring 2 extra minions to be killed along with additional chip damage from the Spitting Scarabs. However, they can be killed rather quickly.
Every other invocation is assumed to be turned on. Consider leaving 'Hardcore run' off while practicing to avoid the expensive death fees.

tasks.name: Something of an expert myself
tasks.description: Complete the Tombs of Amascut raid at level 350 or above without anyone dying.
context: Something of an expert myself is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid at level 350 or above without anyone dying.

tasks.name: Maybe I'm the boss.
tasks.description: Complete a Tombs of Amascut raid with every single boss invocation activated and without anyone dying.
context: Maybe I'm the boss. is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid with every single boss invocation activated and without anyone dying.
method: All boss invocations must be activated to attempt this achievement. This includes invocations that are commonly considered annoying such as Medic!, Keep Back, and Double Trouble. Having all the invocations active will result in a raid level of 310. It is recommended to attempt this task in a group encounter, as Akkha's and Kephri's mechanics are easier to handle in a group. However, decently skilled player shouldn't have much trouble completing this in a solo encounter either.

Akkha is the largest threat in this achievement, as Double Trouble will result in Akkha using two special attacks at once. This is particularly problematic if this rolls into memory and orbs, as the orbs will not expire before the memory quadrants below path level 4. Akkha's other invocations are less of a threat, but by attempting in a group, players may instead get memory and detonation, which is far easier to handle. Player should also be familiar with how to deal with Keep Back invocation before attempting this task, especially if attempting solo.

Fighting Kephri will also be slower since the player has to kill the scarabs that spawn in each charge interlude and have to handle the occasional scarab swarm that appears outside of charging phases. By doing this in a group encounter, Medic! is less of an issue.
Zebak and Ba-Ba are less of a hassle with all of their invocations toggled on, although care should be taken with Upset Stomach, Boulderdash and Mind the Gap.

The other invocations do not need to be toggled, thus allowing the Helpful Spirit to provide full supplies to the player, and all path levels to stay at zero. A normal run (Ba-Ba/Zebak into Kephri) is beneficial for the extra supplies for Akkha in the event of mistakes, as the Wardens should not use too much in most circumstances.

tasks.name: Dropped the ball
tasks.description: Defeat Akkha without dropping any materialising orbs and without dying yourself.
context: Dropped the ball is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Akkha without dropping any materialising orbs and without dying, at raid level 150 or above.
method: This refers to your character spawning the orbs from Akkha's special attack, not the white orbs on the final phase. Stand still during the shadow special to complete the task.

tasks.name: Akkhan't Do it
tasks.description: Defeat Akkha with all Akkha invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying yourself.
context: Akkhan't Do it is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Akkha with all Akkha invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying, at raid level 300 or above. Note that dying and resetting the fight allows multiple retries of this achievement.
method: Using the butterfly method is highly recommended for this method, since Akkha has to be fought with a raid level of 300 or higher.

In solo encounters, the player will have to handle both Memory Blast and Trailing Orbs at once, which when coupled with Akkha's level 4 path levelling results in six iterations of Memory Blast being used. Trailing Orbs can also prove to be daunting as the player will have less tiles to move around as it causes an orb to spawn in front of them after each movement, so players will need to run for the entirety of the attack; fortunately, at such a level, the trailing orbs will end around the fourth blast. Keep Back will also force the player to keep their distance from Akkha in his magic and ranged states, as a melee attack is also launched at the same time with them, which is further compounded by the fact that Akkha walks towards his target regardless of combat style.

Walk the Path is required to reach path level 4. In addition, the Pathmaster invocation is strongly recommended. It is possible for Akkha to reach path level 4 with either Pathseeker or Pathfinder active, but the chances are slim.
If possible, the achievement can be combined with obtaining the Remnant of Akkha as the two requirements overlap, provided that the player can complete the raid at a level of 450 or higher.

tasks.name: No skipping allowed
tasks.description: Defeat Ba-Ba after only attacking the non-weakened boulders in the rolling boulder phase, without dying yourself. The Boulderdash invocation must be activated.
context: No skipping allowed is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba while only destroying uncracked boulders, without dying, and having the Boulderdash invocation active, at raid level 150 or above.
method: This achievement can be easily completed simultaneously along with I'm in a rush.
Create a 150 raid with Boulderdash active.

Prepare by dying repeatedly to farm ~25 honey locusts. This can be sped up with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake. During the boulder phase, you will be tanking boulders in a corner of the room. There are seven boulders in each phase, so fourteen boulders will need to be tanked in total. Each boulder can deal 20 to 27 damage at 150 raid level. 27 damage x 14 boulders = 378 damage, 378/20 healing per Honey locust = ~19 Honey locusts to negate the incoming damage.
Survive both boulder phases by taking full damage, and you will receive both combat achievements.

tasks.name: I'm in a rush
tasks.description: Defeat Ba-Ba after destroying four or fewer rolling boulders in total without dying yourself.
context: I'm in a rush is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba after destroying four or fewer rolling boulders in total without dying, at raid level 150 or above.
method: This achievement can be easily completed simultaneously along with No skipping allowed.
Create a 150 raid (with Boulderdash active if completing along with No skipping allowed).

Prepare by dying repeatedly to farm ~25 honey locusts. This can be sped up with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake. During boulder phase, you will be tanking boulders in a corner of the room. All of them. There are seven boulders in each phase, so fourteen boulders will need to be tanked in total. Each boulder can deal 20 to 27 damage at 150 raid level. 27 damage x 14 boulders = 378 damage, 378/20 healing per Honey locust = ~19 Honey locusts to negate the incoming damage.
Survive both boulder phases taking full damage and you will receive both combat achievements.

tasks.name: Ba-Bananza
tasks.description: Defeat Ba-Ba with all Ba-Ba invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying yourself.
context: Ba-Bananza is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba with all Ba-Ba invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying.

In solo, task is awarded even with multiple deaths, so it is recommended to set invocations to unlimited deaths, so that you can try repeatedly. Set invocations Walk the path and Pathmaster to have a chance to get room to level 4 as the second path. An invocation level of 300 is required to achieve the task, so it is recommended to pick remaining invocations that will not make a difference to completing the task, such as those affecting the Wardens.

If still struggling, you can attempt the monkey room as the third boss (doing two easier ones first) allowing use for ambrosia given by helpful spirit. Double check the monkey path has levelled up to 4 before attempting, as Walk the path is random.

tasks.name: All Praise Zebak
tasks.description: Defeat Zebak without losing a single prayer point. You must also meet the conditions of the 'Rockin' Around The Croc' achievement.
context: All Praise Zebak is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Zebak without losing prayer points at raid level 300 or above, while also satisfying the requirements of Rockin' around the croc achievement.
method: Along with meeting the aforementioned combat achievement, players must not lose a prayer point during the fight. Toggling the Deadly Prayers invocation off can help incase a mistake is made, as the heavy damage that would likely be inflicted from a mistake will result in disqualification.

Players may turn off Invocations that limit the number of attempts as previous deaths against Zebak during the same raid do not affect the task. It is recommended to attempt the achievement on a level 300 raid, with Pathmaster and Walk The Path active to force all bosses to a path level of 3. Then clear the Path of Scabaras, as it uses minimal supplies. There is a 33% chance for the Crondis' path to not level up, as it will be competing with both Apmeken and Het's paths; if this occurs, reset the raid until Crondis' path levels up. Alternatively, one can clear the Path of Apmeken next. The upside to doing so is gaining smelling salts for Zebak which can make the fight significantly easier. The downside is the potential to waste even more time if the Path of Crondis still does not level to 4 after Apmeken, which has a 50% of occurring (giving a ~17% chance overall that Crondis does not level up a single time by the midpoint of the raid).

Bring lots of ranging potions (and optionally super attack and strength) if not using smelling salts. Similarly to Attack, Step, Wait, the achievement is only recorded per attempt, so turning off death invocations will give the player unlimited attempts.

Zebak's attacks will only damage on impact of the player, not when the projectile is launched. At a path level of 4 or above, Zebak has a 5-tick attack cycle, until the enrage phase at which point it becomes a 2-tick attack cycle.

Toggling auto retaliate on as soon as enrage phase is triggered can be very helpful as players can click across the arena when blood spawns. It is advised to turn auto retaliate off for the first 75% of the fight as going out of your weapon's attack range during waves will drag your character.
Rotating your camera angle to have the other side of the arena close to your protect magic and ranged prayers may also be helpful.
If using Runelite, turning metronome on may be helpful; when a magic or ranged attack explodes above your head after Zebak throws it, the damage is calculated exactly 2 ticks later.
Players may also use thralls to increase DPS and may even use the Keris partisan of the sun as neither will fail the task.

tasks.name: Rockin' around the croc
tasks.description: Defeat Zebak with all Zebak invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying yourself.
context: Rockin' around the croc is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Zebak at a path level of 4 with all invocations active without dying, at raid level 300 or above.
method: At a path level of 4, Zebak will attack every 5 ticks (every 3 seconds), increasing to 2 upon triggering the enrage phase (every 1.2 seconds). In addition, his Tidal Waves attack will now only have a single gap, although the waves can still be skipped over with proper experience.

In addition, the Pathmaster invocation is most direct way of levelling Zebak to the level 4 path requirement. It is however possible to get it with both Pathseeker or Pathfinder active - the probability of having Zebak reaching level 4 during such raids is 1/3, and 5/6 respectively.
In solo you can still get the achievement even after dying multiple times.
